text:
maya: heads-up: AcmeTherapy reporting hundreds of 502/504s to hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. sample req-id rq_8a3f9c, customer says it started during a large embedding job (100 items per batch). Anyone seeing edge spike?

 tom: yep, grafana shows p50->p95 latency jump and a spike in edge_502_count around 10:12–10:16 UTC. quick query I ran: `sum(rate(edge_502_count[1m])) by (node)` — concentrated on frontdoor pools.

 alex: digging into logs — upstream auth proxy returning 504s. example from hostedapi logs: `error="upstream request timeout" trace_id=trace-0ff12c`

 eng-sre-bot: deploy event: edge-auth-proxy:v3.4.2 deployed to eu-west-1 at 10:14:22 UTC (CI) — status: success.

 jordan: looks localized to the frontdoor pools handling embed streams. observed midproxy CPU spike and connection pool exhaustion, h2 stream counts maxed. probable fanout amplification from large batch parallelism.

 maya: customer provided repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @batch.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
They see intermittent 502s. batch.json ~100 items, each ~2k tokens.

 sarah: can we try increasing `envoy_upstream_request_timeout` to 30s on a small subset? current default is 15s. also want to check h2 window and max concurrent streams.

 tom: temp workaround idea: per-tenant circuit breaker to reduce fanout parallelism for heavy embed batches. I staged a config on staging; can push a tenant-scoped change for AcmeTherapy only if agreed.

 alex: found more detail in hostedapi error dump — `context deadline exceeded` when contacting auth cache (KV store) while downstream pools are saturated. KV cache hit rate dropped to ~12% during the spike which increased auth lookups. snippet:
```
2024-04-05T10:13:07Z ERROR auth_lookup.go:142 context deadline exceeded req_id=rq_8a3f9c upstream=auth-cache
2024-04-05T10:13:07Z WARN  proxy.go:307 upstream request timeout trace=trace-0ff12c
```

 jordan: I'm preparing a hotfix: backpressure limiter to throttle concurrent embed-stream requests per connection and reduce connection pool pressure. plan: canary 5% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m if metrics look good.

 maya: CC @customer-success-team — I've messaged AcmeTherapy that we're investigating and asked for a list of failing req-ids and exact timestamps. telling them ETA ~30m for mitigation.

 eng-sre-bot: alert action: edge-502-burst rule suppressed for 10m by tom.

 sarah: after canary rollout at 10:28, observed an ~80% drop in 502 rate on affected nodes. still seeing isolated 504s at ingress LB (frontdoor->midproxy). retention: collecting traces for 504s.

 tom: mitigation steps logged: increased h2 max concurrent streams per worker from 100 -> 200 on canary nodes; reduced default embed batch parallelism to 8; PR#4256 contains changes and rollback steps.

 maya: next steps: if stabilized, run a 24h monitoring window and then create a postmortem. action items: (1) add per-tenant rate limits for large-embeds endpoint, (2) add KV cache warmup and better TTLs to avoid auth thundering, (3) review defaults for h2 conn pool sizing. product notified.

 alex: saved traces/req-ids: [rq_8a3f9c, rq_9b7d22, rq_7c1a55] — attaching to the incident ticket.

 jordan: I'll follow up with a config rollout plan and runbook updates.

 maya: thanks everyone — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
